learn.title: Virtual Power Plants — AI Managing Energy
learn.intro: Virtual power plants (VPPs) use AI to coordinate millions of solar panels, batteries, and EVs, acting like a giant utility-scale power plant. This tech stabilizes grids, integrates renewables, and reduces fossil fuel reliance, accelerating the energy transition.
learn.c1_text: AI algorithms predict energy supply from distributed sources, balancing demand in real-time. Like a traffic controller, it routes power from 100,000+ solar rooftops to avoid blackouts.
learn.c2_text: VPPs reduce grid stress by 40% during peak demand, mimicking a traditional power plant’s stability. In Germany, VPPs cut grid congestion by 30%.
learn.c3_text: India’s grid needs 500 GW renewables by 2030. VPPs could manage 250 GW of distributed solar by 2030, easing grid strain.

learn.title: Wind Turbine Lifespan & Blade Recycling
learn.intro: Wind turbines last 20–25 years, but blade disposal poses waste challenges. Innovations in recycling and repurposing blades are critical to making wind energy circular and sustainable.
learn.c1_text: Modern turbines operate 20–25 years, generating 40+ GWh. Regular maintenance extends life, like servicing a car to avoid breakdowns.
learn.c2_text: Glass-fiber blades are hard to recycle. In the US, only 5% are recycled; most end in landfills. New methods use pyrolysis to turn blades into cement additives.
learn.c3_text: India’s first blade recycling plant in Gujarat processes 100+ blades/year. Policy incentives aim to recycle 90% of blades by 2030.

learn.title: Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) Explained
learn.intro: PPAs let companies buy renewable energy directly from producers, bypassing grids. This secures financing for projects and guarantees clean energy supply.
learn.c1_text: A company pays a fixed price (e.g., ₹3.50/kWh) for 10+ years. Like a lease, it funds solar farms without upfront costs.
learn.c2_text: PPAs reduce investor risk. In the US, 80% of wind farms use PPAs. They lock in prices, shielding buyers from market volatility.
learn.c3_text: India’s renewable PPAs grew 30% in 2023. Companies like Tata Power use PPAs to source 2 GW+ solar annually.

learn.title: Wind Turbine Electricity Production
learn.intro: Wind turbines convert kinetic energy from spinning blades into electricity via generators. Aerodynamics and turbine design determine efficiency.
learn.c1_text: Blades act like airplane wings, creating lift. A 100-meter rotor spins at 15 rpm, generating 2–3 MW. Like a fan, but in reverse!
learn.c2_text: The rotor’s shaft spins a generator, converting motion to electricity. Modern turbines use permanent magnets for 95% efficiency.
learn.c3_text: India’s wind farms generate 25 GW, powering 25M homes. Coastal Tamil Nadu leads with 3 GW capacity.

learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar panels on reservoirs or lakes save land, reduce evaporation, and boost efficiency. They’re a game-changer for water-scarce regions.
learn.c1_text: Floating solar uses 70% less land than ground-mounted. In Japan, it reduces reservoir evaporation by 80%, saving 1.5 billion liters/year.
learn.c2_text: Cooling from water increases efficiency by 10%. A 1 MW floatovoltaic system generates 10% more power than land-based.
learn.c3_text: India’s first floating solar in Gujarat’s 1,320 MW solar park saves 150 acres. Policy aims for 10 GW floatovoltaics by 2030.

learn.title: Sodium-Ion Batteries: Affordable Storage
learn.intro: Sodium-ion batteries use abundant sodium instead of lithium, cutting costs by 30–50%. They’re ideal for grid storage and EVs in developing nations.
learn.c1_text: Sodium is 1,000x more abundant than lithium. A sodium-ion battery costs $75/kWh vs. $130/kWh for lithium-ion. Like using table salt instead of rare metals!
learn.c2_text: Sodium-ion batteries offer 160 Wh/kg energy density. They charge faster and last 2,000 cycles, rivaling lithium-ion for grid use.
learn.c3_text: India’s first sodium-ion plant in Tamil Nadu produces 100 MWh/year. Policy targets 500 MWh annual capacity by 2025.
